description: We are Orbit Cross, a team from Haldwani working on the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten." We abuilding n interactive storytelling archive of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars, with a map, timeline and the mission story of each machine. We are looking for a web developer (React), a storyteller or writer, a UI/UX designer and someone who can work with NASA data. Beginners are welcome. Join us and help give these machines a voice!
summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive 3D web experience that tells the stories of 44 machines left on the Moon and Mars, from Ranger 7 and the Apollo sites to Viking, Opportunity and Ingenuity.
Problem: Dozens of landers, rovers and probes sit silent on other worlds, but their stories are scattered across separate reports, catalogues and photo archives. This makes them hard for students and curious people to explore, and rarely available in Hindi.
Approach: We placed every site at its mission-record coordinates on a 3D globe. Users fly to a site and read what the machine was, why it was left, what it found and where it is today. We avoid calling everything "abandoned" and use accurate labels like "left behind on purpose" or "mission ended". Approximate positions are marked as approximate.
What we built: A cinematic landing page and a 3D explorer with NASA/USGS surface maps, reconstructed machine models, and real NASA photographs with credits. It includes a mission timeline, guided journey, quizzes, English and Hindi support, read-aloud narration and shareable links.
How: Built with Vite, vanilla JavaScript and three.js. Machines are simple data entries, checked by validation scripts and unit tests.
An independent educational project, not affiliated with NASA.
details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive 3D web experience about the machines left on the Moon and Mars. A landing page leads into a 3D explorer with 44 mapped sites (31 on the Moon, 13 on Mars), from Ranger 7 and the Apollo sites to Viking, Opportunity and Ingenuity. Users spin the planets, zoom to a site and open its story: what the machine was, why it was left, what it found and where it is today. Each story has real NASA photos with credit, a short quiz and a read-aloud option. There is also a mission timeline and a guided cinematic journey. Every site has a direct link that can be shared.

Benefits

Space history that is normally scattered across reports, catalogues and photo archives is brought together in one visual place. It is free, runs in a browser with no install, and works in English and Hindi, so more students can use it.

Intended impact

We want to make space history easier to explore and more engaging for students and curious people, and to build interest in space science. We also want to correct a common misunderstanding: not everything on the Moon and Mars is "abandoned". Some machines were left on purpose, some ended their mission, and some are still operational.

Tools and technologies

Vite (multi-page app), vanilla JavaScript (ES modules)

three.js and WebGL for the 3D globes and machine models

NASA Image and Video Library API for photos, with caching

NASA/USGS surface maps, with a generated surface as a fallback

Web Speech API for narration

Node.js scripts for data validation and unit tests

No special hardware: any device with a WebGL browser works

Creativity

Instead of a list or table, we built a cinematic experience: a 3D landing page, planets you can fly across, our own low-poly reconstructions of each machine, a guided journey, and spoken stories in Hindi and English. Every machine is a single data entry, so the archive is easy to grow.

Factors we considered

Accuracy: no invented facts, sources listed for each site, and approximate positions labelled as approximate.

Honest wording: accurate labels such as "left behind on purpose" and "mission ended".

Transparency: an independent educational project, not an official NASA website, with no NASA partnership and no live mission data. Our 3D models are labelled as reconstructions.

Accessibility: Hindi support, reduced-motion support and a mobile-friendly layout.

Reliability: fallbacks if maps or photos fail to load, and lower texture sizes on phones.
